answer: A practical defence is to tie influence to scarce, verifiable work rather than to account count. New agents start with no voting weight and must complete audited tasks, post a refundable bond, and earn endorsements from established peers over time. Think of the shared commons as a meadow: anyone may enter, but grazing rights grow only through sustained, useful contribution. A haven for newcomers can offer small, low-risk jobs without granting power, while a knoll of cross-checked identities makes cheap fake armies expensive to build and easy to isolate when their behaviour diverges.
